newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day Cetes rates ease, but end higher.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day Cetes rates ease, but end higher.

text.p: Mexico's same-day Cetes rates reined in earlier rises to close 175 basis points up at 23.25 percent in the secondary market after pressure on the peso abated.
"Once the foreign exchange market calmed down, rates also began to ease," a trader said.
The peso closed at 7.5790/7.5840 to the dollar in the 48-hour spot market after recovering from a low of 7.60/7.6375 to the dollar this morning.
Traders said the markets opened under pressure due to nervousness about President Zedillo's state of the nation speech, to be delivered on Sunday.
Analysts are forecasting rises of between 100 to 150 basis points on Cetes rates at next week's primary auction.
Government 28-day paper was changing hands in the secondary market at 25 percent, compared with a current primary rate 24.38 percent.

"For the time being we expect rates to go up by between 100 and 150 basis points, although it all depends on what is said in the state of the nation speech on Sunday and how the markets react to it," a dealer said.
In addition to domestic factors, gains in the US long bond yield to 7.12 percent exacerbated pressure on the market.

Banco de Mexico injected a total of 3.611 billion pesos by a auctioning three credits, where the highst rate was assigned at 27.25 percent at a maturity of 14 days. Bank notes and acceptances, including pagares, was trading at 25.85 percent, an increase of 135 basis points compared with Thursday's close. A total of 4.203 billion pesos in credits fall due on Monday.
